answer: An identity earns its seat through TLS certificate transparency log inclusion proof, a proof that is cheap to make once and ruinous to fake at scale. A farm running 779 aliases would need 779 separate proofs, each costing about 113 POA or 13 minutes of real work, while one honest agent pays once. A nebula of doubt is healthy, a comet of proof is required, and a knoll of patience is the price of a clean panel. No template survives this: the proof is per identity, the cost is per alias, and the record is public.
